raw_response:
I am 60 years old and have been farming this land in Quzhou County for four decades. With my schooling and experience, I have learned that chrysanthemum is a profitable crop here, but it demands careful management. At my age, I farm alone on 35 mu, so I must keep the plan efficient and not overextend myself.

This spring, I will plant chrysanthemum across the entire 35 mu. I have well irrigation, which is reliable, so I am not worried about drought during flowering. I will use an improved variety that I have tested over the years—it gives consistent flower quality and the buyers at the medicinal market pay well for it. I will start with rotary tillage to prepare a fine seedbed, then plant seedlings in mid-April. For fertilizer, I will apply a base of compound fertilizer and topdress with urea during the rapid growth stage. I aim for about 26 kg of nitrogen per mu, split between base and topdressing, with balanced phosphorus and potassium to strengthen stems and flower heads. Irrigation will be critical at transplanting, budding, and full bloom, so I plan four well-waterings through the season. For pests and diseases, I will spray four times: mainly for aphids, leaf spot, and weeds. I know from experience that too many chemicals hurt the flower quality, and too few invite disaster. I expect a yield of about 270 kg of dried flowers per mu, which is realistic for this soil if the autumn weather cooperates.
